Agent A says: The final grade for module ME2103 includes a 15% contribution from the lab logbook. Logbooks are collected from the mechanical engineering general office and must be signed by a demonstrator before they leave the laboratory. Each entry records the apparatus used, the measurements taken and any deviation from the set procedure. Entries are made in ink, and loose sheets are pasted into the book rather than stapled. Spare logbooks are held at the office counter for anyone who fills one. Laboratory groups are fixed by the general office, and the basement workshop is used.
Agent B says: Twenty-five percent of the final module grade for ME2103 is derived from the lab logbook. Safety induction is required before students may operate the heavy machines in the teaching lab downstairs. Lab coats and goggles are provided by the door, and bags are stowed on wall racks in the corridor outside. Faults with the machines go straight to the technician on duty. Technicians offer drop-in hours alongside each class for questions about the equipment. Students repeating the course stay in their usual class unless they ask to move. Closed shoes are needed in the lab.
Agent C says: The lab logbook accounts for 25% of the final module grade for ME2103. ME2103 is a core module, and its practicals are run in a long room under the main hall. Bench numbers and partner lists are pinned up by the stairs and at the front desk. Kit for each experiment is laid out beforehand and returned to the store afterwards. Everyone works in pairs, and each person keeps a logbook of their own. Benches are numbered, and each pair works at the same bench. Sinks line the far end of the room.
